text:
ana: Follow-up from the console authz + perf RFC. Quick problem statement: authz fanout for dashboard queries is causing tail latency spikes during peak ingest. Proposal idea: a versioned "visibility index" deployed at the query edge that is cheap to consult and can be used as a fast-path to avoid full row-level fanout for most requests.

pranav: Can you sketch the invariants? i.e., when is index authoritative vs advisory?

ana: (typo) ana: Good q. Invariants: 1) index is advisory only — it can answer "definitely-not-visible" and "likely-visible". 2) If index says "definitely-not", we can short-circuit deny. 3) If "likely-visible", we proceed with a lightweight validation or serve a cached snapshot depending on authz latency and staleness budget. 4) Each index has a monotonic version token + last-verified-ts so we can reason about staleness.

yuki: I like version token. How do we avoid data leakage if replication lags? Worst-case: tenant X recently lost access but edge still has an older index showing access.

ana: For safety we bias toward DENY when index age > safe_window. Also each dashboard has metadata opt-in for index-serve. So high-sensitivity dashboards won't use fast-path until we have end-to-end guarantees.

marcos: Operational concerns: memory footprint and invalidation fanout. If we keep per-dashboard visible-tenant lists, that could explode. Any compact representation ideas?

pranav: Consider hierarchical indexes: per-tenant coarse-grain and per-dashboard delta for exceptions. That keeps the common-case cheap. Also compress using varints + run-lengths.

yuki: Another option: keep a tiny LRU cache at the edge keyed by (dashboard_id, tenant_id) present=true with expiry. That avoids global state but increases cache-miss authz calls. Tradeoffs.

ana: Agreed — thinking of hybrid: a small bloom for quick membership test + a versioned exception list for denials (small). Bloom for presence -> route to fast-path; exception list for known revocations -> immediate deny. Bloom false positives are ok, false negatives for exception list must be impossible.

pranav: How do we measure correctness and safety during rollout? Need clear metrics and an abort plan.

marcos: Minimum metrics: `index_age_ms`, `index_hit_ratio`, `fastpath_served_count`, `authz_fanout_reduction_pct`, `stale_denies_count`. Make `stale_denies_count` an alert if > 0.01% of requests. Also `data_leak_incidents` should be a pager block.

yuki: For SLO: prefer serving slightly stale but marked responses over blocking customer flows. UI should show a subtle warning and a manual refresh button. Product ok?

ana: Product approve from me for non-sensitive dashboards. We'll gate by dashboard metadata: `visibility_index: opt_in | opt_out | sensitive`. Defaults to opt_out.

pranav: Rollout plan sketch: 1) implement index read-only at edge with feature flag off, 2) enable on internal tenants only and synthetic traffic to validate correctness, 3) enable canary to 2% external tenants with monitoring, 4) expand if stable.

marcos: Runbook steps if leak suspected: 1) disable index fast-path via flag, 2) invalidate local caches and force authz fanout, 3) trace recent index versions and replication logs, 4) notify security.

ops-bot: ticket created: INFRA-8921 "visibility-index canary + monitoring" assigned to marcos. Canary window 72h.

ana: Example flag JSON I'll add to the RFC draft:
```json
{
  "feature": "visibility_index_fastpath",
  "cohort": "canary",
  "canary_tenants": ["internal-1","tenant-778"],
  "safe_window_ms": "300000",
  "max_index_age_ms": "600000"
}
```

pranav: Nice. Also include a small traffic-splitting header so we can shadow traffic for edge reads vs normal authz to measure divergence: `x-visibility-index-version` and `x-authz-decision-source` (shadow|authz).

yuki: One more thought: make the index monotonic per-dashboard and emit `index_version` in response headers. That makes it easier to correlate stale reads to index versions in logs.

ana: Will add telemetry + headers + runbook to the RFC. I'll draft the short follow-up doc and post for review tomorrow. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
